correctness.rationale: For fixed χ, χ(f^h)=χ^h; only χ with fixed-point cycles can stabilize. Such maps are directed rooted forests. Nonfixed blocks contribute unrestricted independent arrows, fixed blocks contribute (n+1)^(n−1) Cayley forests. Paths give upper and lower sharp indices, with an explicit chain construction for each intermediate index. A multitype labelled exponential construction proves each coefficient. The standalone checker independently compared 2441 small cases and all sharp support/endpoints.

value.rationale: Natural structural question following idempotent criteria: exactly when and how fast can a character-compatible map stabilize? Gives all heights, sharp no-gap interval, a closed product count/probability invariant of fixed-block sizes alone, and a finite coefficient algorithm for every partition profile and every allowed character subsemigroup. This is a general classification rather than a small-instance recomputation.
